result.title: Minimal Memory for Correctable Visual Continuation
result.summary: Given past images and known actions, visual continuation generates future frames from one evolving scene state. Keeping this state revisable matters when an object reappears or a later view changes an earlier interpretation. Once past images cannot be replayed, a summary sufficient for current rendering can lose candidates needed after correction. We establish matching sparse and dense bounds on the bits needed for later correction under stable observations and bounded disagreement. For static streams at the stated smoothness and margin scales, correction incurs at least logarithmic overhead in one dimension and polynomial overhead in higher dimensions. Coherent Archive Memory (CAM) stores geometric summaries with exact updates under clipped expansion and coordinate assignments, then uses historical existence constraints to select one state for all requested frames. Exhaustive photographic tests show strict worst-truth image-risk gains from joint witnesses, while controlled neural continuations recover positions hidden in the current view.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究可修正的视觉延续中，维持可修订场景状态所需的最小记忆，给出稀疏与稠密两种信息论界，并提出按历史存在约束选取单一状态的 Coherent Archive Memory 及相应几何更新与测试。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「后续修正所需比特下界」与保留候选状态的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的信息充分性、纠正后信息坍缩与视觉证据保留提供概念参照；但对象是几何续帧而非语言推理，可供核查迁移边界。
